topic: Eigenvalues of 2x2 Matrices: The DNA of Linear Transformations
target_audience: Undergraduate students in STEM fields (Mathematics, Physics, Engineering)

outline.topic: Eigenvalues of 2x2 Matrices: The DNA of Linear Transformations
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students in STEM fields (Mathematics, Physics, Engineering)

sections.title: Prerequisite & The Core Intuition
sections.content: Start by reviewing a 2x2 matrix as a 'transformer' of 2D space. Introduce 'Leo the Linear Cat,' a character drawn on a 2D grid. When we multiply the grid by a matrix, Leo gets stretched or squashed. Explain that while most points on Leo move to brand new directions, certain 'special' directions stay fixed along their original lines.
sections.example: Visualize Leo the Cat on a grid. Apply a transformation where he is stretched horizontally by 2. His whiskers on the x-axis stay on the x-axis (eigen-direction), while whiskers at 45 degrees tilt toward the horizontal.

sections.title: Defining the Eigen-Relationship
sections.content: Introduce the fundamental equation: Av = λv. Explain that 'A' is the matrix, 'v' is the eigenvector (the direction that doesn't change), and 'λ' (lambda) is the eigenvalue (the scale factor). Emphasize that in this specific direction, matrix multiplication simplifies to simple scalar multiplication.
sections.example: If A maps a vector v to 3v, then λ = 3. This means the 'DNA' of this transformation in that direction is a growth factor of 3.

sections.title: The Characteristic Equation (The Math Tool)
sections.content: Transition from geometry to algebra. To solve Av = λv, we rewrite it as (A - λI)v = 0. Explain that for a non-zero vector 'v' to exist, the matrix (A - λI) must be 'singular,' meaning its determinant must be zero. This leads to the characteristic equation: det(A - λI) = 0.
sections.example: Show a 2x2 matrix with 'λ' subtracted from the top-left and bottom-right diagonal elements, preparing it for the determinant calculation.

sections.title: Step-by-Step Calculation Example
sections.content: Walk through a concrete calculation using a 2x2 matrix. Show the expansion of the determinant into a quadratic equation (the characteristic polynomial) and solve for λ using factoring or the quadratic formula.
sections.example: Matrix A = [[4, 1], [2, 3]]. Calculation: det([[4-λ, 1], [2, 3-λ]]) = (4-λ)(3-λ) - 2 = λ² - 7λ + 10 = 0. Solving (λ-5)(λ-2)=0 gives eigenvalues λ₁=5 and λ₂=2.

sections.title: Visualizing the Resulting Transformation
sections.content: Connect the math back to Leo the Cat. Explain what the specific eigenvalues mean for the shape. If λ > 1, space expands; if 0 < λ < 1, space compresses; if λ is negative, space flips.
sections.example: Animate Leo being stretched 5 times longer along one diagonal (λ=5) and 2 times longer along another (λ=2). This gives a complete 'physical profile' of how the matrix A behaves.

sections.title: Summary & Application
sections.content: Wrap up by highlighting that eigenvalues are used in everything from Google's PageRank algorithm to analyzing the vibration of bridge cables. Reinforce that eigenvalues represent the 'scaling power' of a transformation.
sections.example: A bridge (device) vibrating: its 'natural frequencies' are determined by the eigenvalues of its structural matrix. High eigenvalue = high frequency vibration.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite & The Core Intuition
lecture_lines: Meet Leo, our feline friend on a 2D grid.
Matrices transform space, stretching and squashing everything inside.
Watch Leo distort as we apply a linear transformation.
Most points shift to entirely new directions.
But some special lines stay fixed in their orientation.
animations: Display a 2D coordinate grid (#FFFFFF) with a yellow (#FFFF00) 'Leo the Cat' shape centered.
Apply transformation [[2, 0.5], [0, 1]] to the grid and Leo.
Animate a green vector (#00FF00) along the x-axis, showing it scales but stays on the axis.
Animate a red vector (#FF0000) at 45 degrees, showing it rotates toward the horizontal.
Highlight the green x-axis vector and label it 'Eigen-direction' (#00FF00).

storyboard.title: Defining the Eigen-Relationship
lecture_lines: The relationship is defined as A v equals lambda v.
The eigenvector v stays on its original line.
The eigenvalue lambda scales that vector's length.
animations: Show the equation 'A v = \lambda v' in white (#FFFFFF) at the center.
Change the color of 'A' to blue (#0000FF) and '\lambda' to gold (#FFD700).
Animate a green vector 'v' (#00FF00) scaling by factor 3 with no rotation.

storyboard.title: The Characteristic Equation (The Math Tool)
lecture_lines: To find these values, we rewrite the equation.
Set the determinant of A minus lambda I to zero.
This condition ensures non-zero solutions for our vectors.
animations: Show transition: 'A v = \lambda v' to '(A - \lambda I) v = 0' (#FFFFFF).
Highlight '(A - \lambda I)' with a red (#FF0000) box to show it's a matrix.
Display text 'Matrix must be singular for non-zero v' (#FFFFFF).
Write 'det(A - \lambda I) = 0' in yellow (#FFFF00) with a glowing emphasis.
Show a 2x2 matrix with '\lambda' subtracted from diagonal elements in gold (#FFD700).

storyboard.title: Step-by-Step Calculation Example
lecture_lines: Let's calculate the eigenvalues for this specific matrix.
Subtract lambda from the diagonal elements.
Calculate the determinant to get a quadratic equation.
Solve for lambda to find our two scaling factors.
Here, our eigenvalues are five and two.
animations: Display matrix A = [[4, 1], [2, 3]] and the det calculation setup (#FFFFFF).
Expand determinant to \lambda^2 - 7\lambda + 10 = 0 in yellow (#FFFF00).
Display solutions \lambda_1 = 5, \lambda_2 = 2 in green (#00FF00) with a pulse effect.

storyboard.title: Visualizing the Resulting Transformation
lecture_lines: Let's see how these numbers reshape Leo's world.
An eigenvalue of five expands space along one diagonal.
An eigenvalue of two stretches the other diagonal.
Values above one grow, while values below one shrink.
Negative eigenvalues flip the orientation entirely.
animations: Show Leo the Cat (#FFFF00) on a grid with two green (#00FF00) lines for eigen-directions.
Label the lines '\lambda=5' and '\lambda=2' in green (#00FF00).
Animate Leo stretching by factor 5 along the '\lambda=5' direction.
Animate Leo stretching by factor 2 along the '\lambda=2' direction.
Flash the final shape and display 'The DNA of the Transformation' (#FFFFFF).

storyboard.title: Summary & Application
lecture_lines: Eigenvalues describe the fundamental scaling power of transformations.
They power Google's PageRank and analyze bridge vibrations.
They are the DNA of every linear transformation.
animations: Show icons for 'Google PageRank' and 'Bridge Vibrations' in white (#FFFFFF).
Display text 'Eigenvalues = Scaling Power and Stability' in yellow (#FFFF00).
Fade to black and center a single gold (\lambda) symbol (#FFD700).
